title: Two unknown stems in a practical class
body: During a practical class, Meera cut thin transverse sections of two young stems, labelled P and Q, stained them and observed them under a microscope. In stem P, a few layers of collenchyma lay just below the epidermis. The vascular bundles were arranged in a ring and were separated by a few layers of radially placed parenchyma cells. In each bundle, a thin strip of cambium lay between the xylem and the outer phloem, and the centre of the stem was filled with rounded parenchyma cells having large intercellular spaces. In stem Q, the hypodermis was sclerenchymatous. Numerous vascular bundles were scattered through a large parenchymatous ground tissue, and each bundle was enclosed by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath. Phloem parenchyma was absent and water-containing cavities were seen within the bundles. The bundles near the periphery of Q were smaller than those near its centre.
